finalAssistantText:
I found no 120 s host-tool timeout in the managed omp (`omp/18.6.1`, the binary at `~/.local/share/omp-ui/bin/omp`, dated Oct 5 09:32). The bundled JS shows that a host tool call waits until it is answered, aborted, or the bridge shuts down, with no time limit. ADR-0043 is wrong on this point.

**What I found in the binary** (I pulled the bundled JS out with `strings`):

- **The host-tool bridge has no timer.** `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/rpc/host-tools.ts`, class `RpcHostToolBridge`, method `requestExecution` sends `host_tool_call` and stores the pending call in a map. It settles in only three ways:
  - `handleResult`, when the host answers with `host_tool_result`.
  - The abort signal, which sends `host_tool_cancel` and rejects with `Host tool "X" was aborted`.
  - `close()` / `rejectAllPending()`, when the session shuts down.

  There is no `setTimeout` or `AbortSignal.timeout` anywhere in it. The host-URI bridge (`host-uris.ts`) works the same way.
- **The agent loop has no per-tool timeout.** In `packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts` the only timer is an optional run-level `deadline`, which aborts the whole run with "Deadline exceeded". It is set only from `sdk.ts` `deadline: e.deadline`, and RPC mode never sets it. The `timeout` status counted in `run-collector.ts` is just a telemetry bucket.
- **The `TOOL_TIMEOUTS` table doesn't cover host tools.** `tools/tool-timeouts.ts` lists `bash 300, eval 30, browser 30, computer 120, ssh 60, fetch 20, lsp 20, debug 30, ida 120` (seconds). These apply only to those built-in tools. The "120" in the ADR most likely came from `computer` or `ida`, but that's my guess.
- **None of the other `120000` constants apply.** They belong to the image-question setting, `/loop` condition, hindsight reflect, the changelog model call, mnemopi embed, the title client, IDA, and the tools manager.
- **The RPC timers in `modes/rpc/` don't apply either.** They cover the `ask`/`confirm`/`input` UI dialogs (only when the caller passes `timeout`), the `login`/`predict_word` command timeouts in `wire/commands.ts`, and timers in `rpc-client.ts`. None of them touch host tools.

**What this means for ADR-0043:**
- Line 17: if a host result were dropped, the call would not hang "until omp's own timeout". It would hang until the user aborts the turn or the session closes.
- Lines 51–52: the 60 s watchdog is described as "half omp's own 120 s tool timeout". The reason given is wrong. More importantly, the watchdog is not a backup for an omp timeout: it is the only thing that stops a host tool call from hanging forever. The design still holds, but the ADR should say this.

I only read the code; I didn't run a live test that withholds a host-tool answer and times it. I haven't changed the ADR. If you want it corrected, the fix is to drop the "120 s" claim and describe the watchdog as the only never-hang mechanism.
